clue.text: One needs a doctor in charge of feet

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: Someone with sore feet has to see a doctor who runs the clinic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs' is only a link. The definition is 'of feet', as iambic describes verse written in metrical feet, not anything to do with toes.
explanation.definitionFit: Iambic verse is built from iambs, a metrical foot of one short and one long syllable.

clue.text: One is not intelligent or amusing, unfortunately

definitions.note: read as 'one who is not intelligent', a noun

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone is neither clever nor funny, sadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges OR AMUSING.
explanation.definitionFit: An ignoramus is an ignorant or stupid person.

clue.text: Virile Chinese leader suppressing church

indicators.note: suppressing means the leader holds down the church, containing it

parts.note: Mao Zedong led China

explanation.surface: Chairman Mao, a strong man, cracks down on religion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suppressing' is the container signal: the leader holds the church down inside his name.
explanation.definitionFit: Macho describes aggressive, showy masculinity, so virile.

clue.text: It's on the cards it may precede crisis

definitions.meaning: an ID card shows who the holder is
an ... crisis is confusion about who one is

explanation.definitionFit: Identity cards and identity crisis are both common phrases built on this word.

clue.text: Discharged sailor deceived about victory in Europe

parts.note: AB is an able seaman

indicators.note: about means the word for deceived goes round the other piece

parts.note: to be sold is to be tricked or taken in
VE as in VE Day, Victory in Europe

explanation.surface: A sailor discharged from service was cheated around the time of VE Day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal; VE Day (8 May 1945) marked the Allied victory in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: To be absolved is to be released or set free from guilt or obligation, as discharged means.

clue.text: Steamy habitat is developed? It's of no importance

indicators.note: developed suggests the letters have grown into something new, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off whether a humid habitat has been built on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' rearranges STEAMY HABITAT; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is said to dismiss a point as not mattering, much like saying it is unimportant.

clue.text: Supplication of squadron leader among stars

indicators.note: among places that letter inside the stars

parts.note: Orion is a constellation of stars

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of squadron

explanation.surface: A squadron leader among the stars prays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' gives S, and 'among' puts it inside ORION.
explanation.definitionFit: An orison is an old word for a prayer, a supplication to God.

clue.text: Verse on executed European upstart

indicators.note: executed means beheaded, so the first letter goes

parts.note: a Bulgarian is a European

explanation.surface: Verses about a European upstart who was put to death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'executed' means beheaded: BULGARIAN loses its head to give ULGARIAN, under V ('on' in a down clue).
explanation.definitionFit: A vulgarian is a coarse, ostentatious person, often newly rich, like an upstart.

clue.text: Duplicate alteration to end of song

indicators.note: alteration to end of means the final letter of the song is changed

parts.note: a ditty is a simple song

explanation.surface: A copy is made with a change to how a song finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alteration to end of' changes the last letter of DITTY, Y, to O.
explanation.definitionFit: Ditto means the same again, a duplicate of what came before.

clue.text: Laughs quietly, underwear being mentioned

indicators.note: being mentioned signals that the word is spoken, so we want its sound

parts.note: knickers are women's underpants

explanation.surface: Someone giggles when the subject of underwear comes up.
explanation.walkthrough: The silent K of KNICKERS vanishes when said, leaving a word sounding identical.
explanation.definitionFit: To snicker or nicker is to give a quiet, suppressed laugh.

clue.text: Ends up with class displaying excessive neatness

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: tips are ends
and means with
polish is refinement or class

explanation.surface: Someone finishes up with a class of fussily tidy people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns TIPS into SPIT; 'displaying' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Spit and polish is the military habit of obsessive cleaning, so extreme neatness.

clue.text: One of several arriving together seen as impediment on outing

indicators.note: on in an across clue means the impediment is written after the outing

parts.note: a trip is an outing or excursion
a let is an obstruction, as in 'without let or hindrance'

explanation.surface: A hold-up on a day trip is seen as one of several things arriving together.
explanation.walkthrough: LET as hindrance is an old legal sense, also used in tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: A triplet is one of three children born at the same birth, so arriving together.

clue.text: Resting-place supervisor initiated in part of plant

indicators.note: in means the initial letter goes inside the plant part

parts.note: the root is the underground part of a plant

indicators.note: initiated means only the start of the word supervisor is taken

explanation.surface: A supervisor gets started in a resting-place among the plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initiated' gives S, the first letter of 'supervisor', and 'in' places it inside ROOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A roost is a place where birds settle to rest at night.

clue.text: He loves to win a moratorium for a bit

indicators.note: for a bit says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone is keen to secure a temporary suspension of payments.
explanation.definitionFit: An inamorato is a male lover, so a man who loves someone.

clue.text: Male and Italian, I'm deployed as a reservist

indicators.note: deployed suggests the troops of letters are spread out into a new formation

explanation.surface: An Italian man joins up as a reserve soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deployed' rearranges M, ITALIAN and IM into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A militiaman serves in a militia, a reserve force of citizen soldiers rather than regulars.

clue.text: Without hesitation Sir Edwin frames better painting

indicators.note: frames means the shortened name surrounds the other piece
without means the hesitation is removed from the name

parts.note: Sir Edwin Landseer was a Victorian painter
er is the sound of hesitation
to cap is to better or outdo

explanation.surface: Sir Edwin unhesitatingly puts a frame round a superior painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' removes the hesitation from the painter's surname and 'frames' is the container signal; Landseer painted the Monarch of the Glen.
explanation.definitionFit: A landscape is a painting of natural scenery.

clue.text: Tragic queen recalled girl in 8

indicators.note: in places the reversed name inside the abbreviation

parts.note: 8-down is ditto, abbreviated DO

indicators.note: recalled means the girl's name is called back, read backwards

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana

explanation.surface: A tragic queen remembers a girl in clue 8.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns DI into ID, and 'in' puts it inside DO, the usual abbreviation for ditto (the answer to 8 down).
explanation.definitionFit: Dido, Queen of Carthage, killed herself when Aeneas abandoned her, a classic tragic heroine.

clue.text: Scoffed too much regarding school report

parts.note: over can mean regarding, as in a dispute over money

indicators.note: report signals a sound, so the school's name is said aloud

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: Someone ate too much while fretting over their school report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'report' is not a school report but a sound cue: ETON said aloud gives EATEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To have overeaten is to have eaten more than enough, gorged.

clue.text: Fish in can consumed by singular poet

indicators.note: consumed by means the can is swallowed inside the other letters

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
Thomas Gray wrote the Elegy in a Country Churchyard
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A fish from a can is eaten by a remarkable poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consumed by' is the container signal: the can is eaten up inside the singular poet.
explanation.definitionFit: A stingray is a flat fish with a venomous spine on its tail.

clue.text: Smooth woman writer Chopin loved

definitions.meaning: to smooth wood is to rub it with sandpaper
George ..., the French novelist, was Chopin's lover

explanation.definitionFit: George Sand was the pen name of the novelist who lived with Chopin; sanding makes a surface smooth.

clue.text: Right to enter a social function without glove

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the dance goes round the glove

parts.note: a dance is a social gathering
a mitt is a mitten or glove

explanation.surface: Entry to a party is refused to anyone not wearing gloves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, a common crossword container signal, not 'lacking'.
explanation.definitionFit: Admittance is permission or the right to go into a place.

clue.text: Involve volunteer troops in border rising

indicators.note: in places the troops inside the turned word
rising in a down clue means the word reads upwards

parts.note: a line is a border or boundary
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: Volunteer soldiers get caught up in a revolt on the frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' reverses the border word upwards, as this is a down clue; 'in' is the container signal. The Territorial Army is Britain's part-time volunteer force.
explanation.definitionFit: To entail is to involve something as a necessary consequence.

clue.text: Deceive pupils following offence on motorway

indicators.note: on in an across clue means the offence comes after the motorway
following means the pupils come after the offence

parts.note: MI is the M1, Britain's first motorway, written as letters
a sin is an offence or wrongdoing
a form is a school class of pupils

explanation.surface: Pupils lie to cover up a driving offence on the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 motorway is written MI in crosswords. FORM is a British word for a school class.
explanation.definitionFit: To misinform is to give someone false information, which deceives them.

clue.text: Ridicules trial examinations

definitions.meaning: to mock is to make fun of
British practice exams sat before the real ones

explanation.definitionFit: Mocks are both scornful taunts and, in Britain, the practice exams pupils take before finals.

clue.text: Informer disturbed by current gossip

indicators.note: disturbed by means the informer is broken into by the other piece

parts.note: a nose is slang for a police informer
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A grass is upset by the latest rumours going round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed by' puts I inside NOSE. NOSE as informer is British criminal slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Noise can mean common talk or rumour, as in noises being made about something.

clue.text: Hibernian flag seen over hospital

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the plant sits above the hospital

parts.note: a flag is a type of iris plant

explanation.surface: An Irish flag is seen flying over a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flag' is not a banner but the yellow flag, a wild iris.
explanation.definitionFit: Hibernia is the Latin name for Ireland, so Hibernian means Irish.

clue.text: Sort of bread a bloke takes early in afternoon

parts.note: a chap is a man or bloke
at one o'clock, AT I, is early in the afternoon

explanation.surface: A man has his bread roll early in the afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' is a link. 'early in afternoon' is read as 'at one' (one o'clock), written AT I with the Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapati is a flat unleavened Indian bread, so one kind of bread.

clue.text: Funny story about king by one supporting royal house

indicators.note: about means the rearranged story goes round the other letters
funny signals the letters of story are treated oddly and rearranged
by places one beside the king

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A comic tale about a king by someone loyal to the royal family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funny' turns STORY into YORST, and 'about' puts K and I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A Yorkist backed the House of York in the Wars of the Roses.

clue.text: Bird initially terribly timid without being furtive

indicators.note: without means outside, so the timid word goes around the rest

parts.note: shy means timid
a teal is a small duck

indicators.note: initially means only the first letter of terribly is used

explanation.surface: A bird is terribly timid without being sneaky about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not 'lacking', and 'initially' takes the first letter of 'terribly'; 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealthy means acting quietly and secretly, the same as furtive.

clue.text: A short line from Weston-super- Mare

definitions.text: A short line from Weston-super- Mare

parts.words: A short line from Weston-super- Mare
parts.note: not a train route out of the seaside town but the little dash printed in its name

explanation.walkthrough: Weston-super-Mare is an English seaside town; the 'short line' sounds like a branch railway.
explanation.definitionFit: The short horizontal mark joining parts of a compound name such as Weston-super-Mare is this punctuation mark.
